ashley: Quick ask — running a sharded inference run across 8 A100s to repro a perf regression. Want to capture nsys + torch.profiler traces from the same workload so we can compare flamegraphs. Can someone sanity-check my capture plan and flags?

max: +1. paste what you're planning to run. main concerns: trace size and syncing start across ranks.

ashley: Plan below. trying to keep it minimal: 1 warmup step, 3 capture steps. nvtx around model forward + kv cache update. upload to shared bucket after scrub.

```bash
# launcher (slurm-ish / mpirun wrapper)
nsys profile --output=/tmp/run_rank${RANK} --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=nvtx_tag:start --capture-range-end=nvtx_tag:end \
  python -m torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 run_infer.py --batch 1 --seq 1024
```

# inside code
with torch.profiler.profile(use_cuda=True, record_shapes=True, profile_memory=True) as p:
    with torch.autograd.profiler.emit_nvtx():
        nvtx.mark("start")
        outputs = model(input)
        nvtx.mark("end")

# after run: tar up /tmp/run_rank* and gsutil cp to gs://redwood-traces/tmp/ashley-1892345678.tar.gz
```

leo: A couple quick notes:
- capture-range nvtx can be finicky across ranks; recommend using a fixed epoch/step barrier so all ranks start capture within ~100ms of each other.
- set NSYS_DISABLE_METRICS=0? And set NSYS_RECORDER_LIMIT to avoid infinite growth.
- use `--trace` flags you listed but add `--sample=none` if you don't want sampling overhead.

max: Also, size-wise, 8 ranks x 3 steps with full cuda events + kernel traces can be HUGE (>10GB). Suggest: 1) reduce captured ops by wrapping only the block you care about, 2) run on a smaller sequence length to get representative hotspots, 3) if you only need cpu timeline + nvtx, drop some cuda metrics.

ashley: Good call. I can reduce to seq 512 for capture. For the start sync, I'll insert `dist.barrier()` right before nvtx start tag. Is there a recommended env var for recorder limit?

leo: Try `NSYS_RECORDER_HEAP_SIZE=200000000` (200MB) and `NSYS_RECORDER_BUFFER_SIZE=4000000` — those helped us in past traces. Also `--force-overwrite` so partial uploads don't block.

maya: If you want me to look after upload, I can scrub hostnames and any customer IDs. Please redaction checklist: remove any plaintext dataset paths, API keys, and replace node hostnames with node-XX. I recommend this simple scrub script before tar: 

```bash
# scrub.sh
find . -type f -name "*.log" -exec sed -i -E 's/(user|project)=[^\s]+/project=REDACTED/g' {} +
python -c "import os;print('rename hostnames')"
# replace obvious hostnames
for f in $(grep -R --line-number "$HOSTNAME" . | cut -d: -f1 | uniq); do sed -i 's/$HOSTNAME/node-XX/g' $f; done
```

ashley: thanks — I'll run scrub and upload. question: should I include torch.profiler trace files (.pt.trace?) or just nsys output?

max: include both if you can. torch.profiler has useful operator-level stacking that maps to python lines. nsys gives kernel-level timing. For flamegraphs we usually convert nsys to collapsed stacks with nsight tools then aggregate.

trace-bot: Uploaded artifact: gs://redwood-traces/ashley/1892345678/ashley-8xA100-seq512.tar.gz (size: 2.1GB). Access: internal-only.

maya: I pulled the tar and ran quick `nsys stats` and `nsys export` to flamegraph. Looks like heavy time in fused attention kernel on rank 3 and 6. I'll post a quick flamegraph screenshot in a follow-up thread.

ashley: awesome, appreciate it. maya @maya can you also run a kv-cache miss trace? I want to see if cache writes are the bottleneck.

maya: yes — run the same capture but instrument the cache update block with `nvtx.mark('kv_write_start')`/`nvtx.mark('kv_write_end')` and send me the result. I'll overlay timelines.

max: small FYI — when you attach the tar to an incident or ticket, note the exact capture flags and commit hash. makes it much easier to reproduce.

ashley: will do. tagging this as done for now — I'll open a follow-up once I have the kv trace. Thanks everyone :tada:

leo: thx! feel free to ping if the upload link perms need adjustment.

trace-bot: Note: retention for /ashley/1892345678 set to 30 days.

maya: short follow-up — flamegraph shows one hot stack dominated by `attention_cuda::forward` -> `attention_cuda::fused_query_key` which lines up with the model change in PR #4127. cc @max.

max: nice find — I'll add that to the perf regression thread and queue a microbench for that kernel.

ashley: closing this thread for now. will post results when microbench completes.
